nl.statement: A normalized overcomplete independent-component observational world. Fix an observed dimension \(p\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\) and a source dimension \(n\in\{p,p+1,\ldots\}\), with index sets \(\mathsf O=\{1,\ldots,p\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\mathsf L=\{p+1,\ldots,n\}\), and an ordered pair of observed coordinates \(x\in\mathsf O\), \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\). The data-generating objects are a mixing matrix \(C=[c_1\;\cdots\;c_n]\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and a source vector \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n)^\top\in\mathbb R^n\) with mutually independent, nondegenerate, non-Gaussian coordinates; the observed vector is \(X=C\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^p\) and the observational law is \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^p)\). For a lifting degree \(d\ge1\), a contraction degree \(q\ge1\) and the common order \(r=2d+q\), the source cumulant vector is \(\lambda_j=\operatorname{cum}_r(\varepsilon_j)\), the observational cumulant tensor is \(\mathcal T_r=\operatorname{cum}_r(X)=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_jc_j^{\otimes r}\in\operatorname{Sym}^r(\mathbb R^p)\), and the lifted direction matrix is \(V_d=[c_1^{\otimes d}\;\cdots\;c_n^{\otimes d}]\in\mathbb R^{p^d\times n}\); two unit probes \(u,v\in\mathbb S^{p-1}\) are fixed, and \(\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\) indexes the representation. The law-level direction object is \(\mathcal D(P_X)\subseteq\mathbb P^{p-1}\), the union of the unordered projective column sets of every irreducible, all-non-Gaussian independent-component representation of \(P_X\). — Reuse inside this block: `Causalean.Stat.MomentProblems.sourceCumulant` for \(\lambda_j=\operatorname{cum}_r(\varepsilon_j)\); `Causalean.Stat.MomentProblems.IsGaussianLaw` for the non-Gaussianity atom; `ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun` for mutual independence; `Matrix.rank` / `Matrix.det` / `Matrix.submatrix` for the rank and deletion-minor vocabulary. NEW here: the order-\(r\) MULTIVARIATE cumulant tensor -- Causalean's `jointCumulant` is bivariate only (`Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/MomentProblems/Cumulant.lean:60`), so the tensor \(\mathcal T_r\) is built inline per D-A as a symmetric array `(Fin r -> Fin p) -> Real` defined by the same set-partition Moebius formula. Bypass-justified for `Causalean/Graph/SWIG.lean` and `Causalean/SCM/Model/SCM.lean`: this world has no DAG and no kernel-valued mechanism, only a linear map \(C\) and an independent source vector.

The source-minimal cyclic structural-completion world attached to the observational world. A completion of the fixed representation is a pair \(\mathcal M=(Q,H)\) of real \(n	imes n\) matrices whose endogenous equilibrium \(V\in\mathbb R^n\) solves \(QV=H\varepsilon\), with \(Q=I_n-B\) unit-diagonal, \(H\) monomial (exactly one nonzero entry in each row and each column, so exactly one disturbance per equation), \(\det(Q)

e0\) and a hard-intervention equilibrium effect \(	heta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=(Q^{-1})_{yx}/(Q^{-1})_{xx}\). At the law level a completion \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}=(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}},Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}},H^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}},\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})\) with \(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\ge p\) has equilibrium \(V^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\), observed mixing matrix \(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=[(Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})^{-1}H^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}]_{\mathsf O,:}\), law-assigned source \(s^{\mathrm{law}}_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\), reference-aligned source \( ar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\), and observed response vector \(ho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})\in\mathbb R^{p-1}\); the source-minimal observational-law fiber \(\mathfrak F^{\mathrm{law}}_x(P_X)\) collects those completions that reproduce \(P_X\) with irreducible \(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) and independent nondegenerate non-Gaussian coordinates of \(\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\). No spectral-radius or dynamical-stability restriction is imposed. — Bypass-justified against the whole Causalean causal substrate, one line per surveyed module: `Causalean/SCM/Model/SCM.lean` (generalized SCM = node-indexed kernels over a DAG) -- this world is a single linear system \(QV=H\varepsilon\) that is deliberately CYCLIC, so no DAG exists; `Causalean/Graph/SWIG.lean` and `Causalean/SCM/Do/*` (do-calculus, SWIG splits) -- the hard intervention here is the deletion of row/column \(x\) from \(Q\), an algebraic minor condition, not a graph surgery; `Causalean/SCM/ID/Identifiable.lean` (`Identifiable G Phi` quantifies over `Causalean.SCM` models sharing a `SWIGGraph`) -- the identification statements here quantify over a fiber of MATRIX TUPLES sharing an observational law, with no shared graph; `Causalean/SCM/ID/{Adjustment,Backdoor,Frontdoor,BackdoorCriterion}.lean` and `GraphicalThms/*` -- no adjustment set, backdoor set or c-component appears anywhere in the note; `Causalean/SCM/ID/Overlap.lean` -- the note's sampling model states treatment overlap is not applicable. The deletion-rank frontier and its constructive certificate. For the fixed mixing matrix \(C\) and treatment coordinate \(x\), the deletion-rank-admissible source set is \(J_x(C)=\{j\in\mathsf S:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\}\); the induced scalar and vector frontiers are \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)=\{C_{yj}/C_{xj}:j\in J_x(C)\}\subseteq\mathbb R\) and \(\mathcal V_x(C)=\{(C_{ij}/C_{xj})_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}:j\in J_x(C)\}\subseteq\mathbb R^{p-1}\). The certificate fixes one basis extension \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\) of the rows of \(C\) (so \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\)) with inverse \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\), reads admissibility off the kernel block \(K_x=(W_0)_{:,\{x\}\cup\mathsf L}\), and, for each \(j\in J_x(C)\), produces by one latent-row shear and one alternating-path flip of a single column-saturating matching a completion \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)_j=\mathcal M_j=(Q_j,H_j)\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) whose equation \(x\) is driven by source \(j\). — Search trace: grep -i 'deletion|admissible|frontier' over ../Causalean and CausalSmith/CausalSmith -> the only hits are `CausalSmith/ExactID/EID_RobustBackshiftUniformDistance_Research/{TUniformSupportDeletionRadius,TGenericSupportFrontier}.lean`, which speak of support deletion for a SQUARE `RealMatrix p` backShift system with environment-indexed shifts (`Basic.lean:19 abbrev RealMatrix (p : Nat) := Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real`) -- bypass-justified: no rectangular \(p\times n\) overcomplete mixing, no per-source column deletion, no environments here; but its `Helpers/MatrixMargins.lean` and `Helpers/ConfidenceUnion.lean` are the closest structural template and are recorded as F3 references. Mathlib-side: `lean_leansearch` 'nonzero determinant gives a permutation with all matrix entries nonzero; bipartite perfect matching from Hall' -> `SimpleGraph.exists_isPerfectMatching_of_forall_ncard_le`, `SimpleGraph.exists_bijective_of_forall_ncard_le` (Hall), `Matrix.nondegenerate_iff_det_ne_zero`; the note's proof extracts matchings from a nonzero Leibniz term, so `Matrix.det_apply` + `Finset.exists_ne_zero_of_sum_ne_zero` is the direct route and Hall is the fallback. `Matrix.vandermonde` supplies the worst-case dense-output instance of D-B.

The separated common-order i.i.d. inference world. Fix a miscoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and margins \(a,\delta,\sigma\in(0,1]\), \(0<\kappa\le\Lambda\), \(M\ge1\). The separated class \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) collects the tuples \(\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\) with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), \(r=2d+q\), \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\) satisfying the source, normalization, cumulant-magnitude, probe-orientation, lifted-rank, pencil-gap, moment-envelope, mixing-singular, loading-selection and deletion-rank conditions. The explicit local-inversion constants are \(\eta=\kappa\sigma^{q+2}\), \(\chi=\sqrt n/\sigma\), \(h=2/\eta+2n\Lambda/\eta^2\), \(\epsilon_0=\min\{\eta/2,\sigma/(6\chi h)\}\), \(L_z=nh\{2\chi+6n\Lambda\chi^2/(\eta\sigma)\}\), \(L_C=2\sqrt{np}L_z\), and the tensor-pencil inverse maps \(\mathcal T_r\) back to \(\{c_1,\ldots,c_n\}\) through the contractions \(M_w\), the compressions \(G_w=A_wA_u^{-1}\) and the spectral projectors of \(G_v\). The data are \(N\) independent draws \(\mathbf X_N=(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(N)})\) from \(P_X\); from them one forms the clipped empirical cumulant tensor \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_r\) at clipping level \(B_m=1+H\) with \(H=n^{2r}\max\{1,M\}\) and \(m=\binom{p+r}{r}-1\), the minimum-distance fit \(\widehat C\), the estimated set \(\widehat J_x=J_x(\widehat C)\), and, with \(e_N=\sqrt{m(1+H)/(N\alpha)}\), \(\tau_N=L_me_N\), \(b_N=2L_C\tau_N\), \(w_N=(a^{-1}+a^{-2})b_N\) and \(w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}=\sqrt{p-1}\,w_N\), the scalar confidence union \(\mathcal U_{xy}\subseteq\mathbb R\) and the response-vector confidence union \(\mathcal U_x^{\mathrm{vec}}\subseteq\mathbb R^{p-1}\). — This is the block with the most confirmed reuse. `Causalean.Mathlib.Probability.iid_mean_euclidean_abs_le` (../Causalean/Mathlib/Probability/IidMeanVariance.lean:318) and `memLp_two_iid_mean_euclidean` give the vector empirical-mean L2/L1 deviation used at (14)-(15); `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.abs_singularValues_add_sub_singularValues_le_opNorm` (SingularValueWeyl.lean:212) and its `ContinuousLinearMap` form (line 228) are exactly the Weyl step (20) `|s_min(G') - s_min(G)| <= ||G'-G||_op`; `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.singularValues_mul_mul_transpose_lower_bound` (RectangularSignalSingularValues.lean:179) is exactly the `s_min(S D S^T) >= s_min(S)^2 s_min(D)` step (4) of the local-inverse lemma; The minimum-distance fit does NOT reuse `Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory.borelMeasurable_compact_argmin_selector` (CompactArgminSelection.lean:134): that decl returns an arbitrary measurable feasible minimizer with ties unresolved, whereas def:minimum-distance-fit is the lexicographically selected minimizer, which this block constructs and verifies locally by successive coordinate argmin over the compact feasible set (`IsCompact.exists_isMinOn`, Mathlib.Topology.Order.Compact). `Metric.hausdorffDist` (Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffDistance) is the `d_H` of the theorem. Analogous module for the perturbation layer: `Causalean/Discovery/LinearDisentanglement/Quantitative/` -- `opNorm_sub_le_of_approximate_simultaneous_congruence`, `transition_coordinate_product_control`, `admissibleRadius`, `stabilityConstant` carry the SAME proof pattern (explicit local operator-norm modulus + admissible residual radius for an approximate simultaneous congruence) at a second-moment/congruence abstraction; the gap to bridge is that the present pencil is an order-\(r\) tensor contraction with a Riesz-projector eigenvector step rather than a family of congruences. The heterogeneous-order population-oracle world. Given the observational law \(P_X\), the known source count \(n\) and an integer cap \(K\ge2n-1\), the coupled recovery handle \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{multi}}(P_X,n;K)\) processes each order \(
u\in\{2n-1,\ldots,K\}\): it forms \(\mathcal T_
u(P_X)=\operatorname{cum}_
u(X)\), reshapes it into the three blocks of degrees \((n-1,n-1,
u-2n+2)\), takes the least \(R\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) for which the reshaped tensor admits a decomposition into \(R\) nonzero terms \(\gamma_h\operatorname{vec}(z_h^{\otimes\ell_1})\otimes\operatorname{vec}(z_h^{\otimes\ell_2})\otimes\operatorname{vec}(z_h^{\otimes\ell_3})\), retains the projective classes \([z_h]\) of any minimizer, unions them across processed orders by exact projective equality, and returns once that union has cardinality \(n\). This is a population-oracle description with exact cumulants, not a finite-sample algorithm. — Search trace: grep -i 'tensor|rank decomposition|CP rank' over ../Causalean -> nothing at the tensor-decomposition abstraction (`Data.Holor` in Mathlib gives `CPRankMax` but no uniqueness).  =\sum_{h=1}^{R}\gamma_h

\[
 \mathcal D(P_X)=\{[c_j]:j\in\mathsf S\}.
\]
This is a full-law identification statement, not an evaluation algorithm. Moreover, \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\), every \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) has \(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n\), and the sharp law-fiber response-vector set is
\[
 \left\{\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}):\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\right\}
 =\mathcal V_x(C)
 =\left\{\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\right\}.
\]
For every ordered \(y\ne x\), its scalar coordinate projection is exactly
\[
 \left\{[\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})]_y:\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\right\}
 =\mathcal R_{xy}(C).
\]
The frontiers are independent of the representative of \(\mathcal D(P_X)\), because column permutation and nonzero rescaling leave them invariant. The entire response vector is identified if and only if \(\mathcal V_x(C)\) is a singleton, and the \(y\)-coordinate effect is identified if and only if \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) is a singleton. If the latter is not a singleton, two indices with distinct ratios yield two exact same-law SCM countermodels via the canonical embeddings \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\) of the shared-kernel and shared-matching certificate construction. Conditional on any exact irreducible mixing representative \(C\), all frontier values and one exact witness per value are computable in \(O(n^3)\) exact real-arithmetic operations. This order is optimal for dense all-witness output in the worst case. This is not an end-to-end complexity claim for obtaining \(C\) from \(P_X\). No stability assumption is imposed.

They can be constructed in \(O(n^3)\) additional arithmetic operations after the shared basis extension and inverse. For every \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\), the scalar coordinate \([\rho_x]_y\) is point identified over the same law fiber if and only if
\[
 |\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 \operatorname{rank}\!\left(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\right)=1.
\]
If this scalar criterion fails, two canonical witnesses have distinct \(y\)-coordinate responses. Each scalar frontier is the corresponding coordinate projection of \(\mathcal V_x(C)\); the claim does not combine coordinates arising from different source indices into a response vector.

 \lVert c_j\rVert_2=\lVert c'_j\rVert_2=1,
 \qquad
 \kappa\le |\lambda_j|,|\lambda'_j|\le\Lambda,
 \qquad
 u^\top c_j,u^\top c'_j\ge\sigma.
\]
Suppose also that both lifted matrices \([c_1^{\otimes d}\;\cdots\;c_n^{\otimes d}]\) and \([(c'_1)^{\otimes d}\;\cdots\;(c'_n)^{\otimes d}]\) have least singular value at least \(\sigma\), and that both ratio collections
\[
 \left\{\frac{v^\top c_j}{u^\top c_j}:j\in\mathsf S\right\},
 \qquad
 \left\{\frac{v^\top c'_j}{u^\top c'_j}:j\in\mathsf S\right\}
\]
have pairwise gaps at least \(\sigma\). Define
\[
 \mathcal T(C,\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_jc_j^{\otimes r},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T(C',\lambda')=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda'_j(c'_j)^{\otimes r}.
\]
If \(\lVert\mathcal T(C',\lambda')-\mathcal T(C,\lambda)\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\), then there is a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\mathsf S\) such that
\[
 \lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F
 \le L_C\lVert\mathcal T(C',\lambda')-\mathcal T(C,\lambda)\rVert_F.
\]
In particular, this bound applies to two numerical factor pairs in the feasible set of the separated tensor minimum-distance fit; no source law for the fitted pair is required.
